solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Commentator’s dread: champ producing masses of data?

indicators.note: a commentator speaks, so the words are to be taken by their spoken sound

blocks.note: terror is dread; said in a non-rhotic accent it matches the metric prefix
to champ is to bite; the computing unit is said the same way

explanation.surface: A sports commentator's nightmare is a champion who generates mountains of statistics.
explanation.walkthrough: In British speech 'terror' and 'tera' sound alike because the final R is silent.
explanation.definitionFit: A terabyte is a unit of a trillion bytes, so it describes very large quantities of stored information.

clue.text: Record fifth beer-pump?

blocks.note: a tap dispenses beer
E is the fifth letter, so a fifth tap in a lettered row would be tap E

explanation.surface: A bar with a fifth beer engine to record.
explanation.walkthrough: Lettering a row of taps A, B, C, D, E makes the fifth one 'tap E', which is why the letter follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Tape is a recording medium, and to tape something is to record it.

clue.text: Bank assistance — pounds I will withdraw

indicators.note: withdrawing means leaving, so those letters drop out of the word

blocks.note: relief is assistance to those in need
L is the abbreviation for pounds sterling, from libra
taken as written

explanation.surface: A bank offers financial help, but the money is about to be taken away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bank' looks financial, but here it is an underwater ridge.
explanation.definitionFit: A reef is a ridge of rock or coral near the surface of the sea, a bank in that sense.

clue.text: Runs out of gap on river in swimsuit?

definitions.note: the question mark marks a swimsuit as one example of the answer

indicators.note: taking something out of a word removes it, so that letter goes

blocks.note: a breach is a gap, as in a wall
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs
the Wear is a river in north-east England

explanation.surface: Someone in a swimming costume dashes out through a gap beside a river.
explanation.walkthrough: The Wear flows through Durham and Sunderland.
explanation.definitionFit: A swimsuit is one item of clothing worn at the seaside, so it exemplifies the category.

clue.text: Greeting PM?

blocks.note: first meaning: to pass this phrase is to exchange a polite hello
second meaning: afternoon is one part of the day, as a clock or a question about the hour gives

explanation.walkthrough: PM looks like the Prime Minister, but it is post meridiem, afternoon; 'pass the time of day' is an idiom for a brief friendly chat.
explanation.definitionFit: Giving someone the time of day is a basic acknowledgement, and afternoon is literally one period of a day.

clue.text: Broadway musical, The King and I, by a small opera company

blocks.note: K is the chess and card abbreviation for king
taken as written
S is the clothing-size abbreviation for small
the Met is New York's Metropolitan Opera

explanation.surface: A list of Broadway musicals, The King and I among them, being staged by a little opera troupe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The King and I' looks like the title of another musical, but it is just K plus I.
explanation.definitionFit: Kismet is a 1953 stage musical that played on Broadway, with songs adapted from Borodin.

clue.text: Adult insect? The writer’s not entirely enthralled

indicators.note: not the whole word means the final letter is cut off

blocks.note: the writer is the setter, I, and with 'is' becomes I'M
agog means eagerly enthralled

explanation.surface: An author confesses to being only half gripped by a grown-up bug.
explanation.definitionFit: Imago is the biological term for the final, sexually mature stage of an insect after metamorphosis.

clue.text: Second barbed comment? I fix upset artist

indicators.note: in a down clue upset means turned upside down, so the letters read bottom to top

blocks.note: a mo is a moment, a second
a dig is a sly jibe
taken as written
to nail is to fix in place

explanation.surface: After a second sharp remark, someone vows to sort out an upset painter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' looks like an anagram signal, but in this down clue it simply turns both the pronoun and the fixing word upside down.
explanation.definitionFit: Amedeo Modigliani was an Italian painter and sculptor famed for elongated portraits.

clue.text: Locomotive to fail: no good stopping German one

indicators.note: something stopping a gap plugs it, so it sits inside the other word

blocks.note: to tank is to flop badly
eine is German for one, feminine form
NG is the abbreviation for no good

explanation.surface: A train set to break down because a useless part is blocking a German unit.
explanation.definitionFit: A tank engine is a steam locomotive carrying its water in tanks on the engine itself rather than a tender.

clue.text: French are getting behind petition to host one group of stars

indicators.note: a host takes a guest in, so one word is placed inside the other

blocks.note: to plead is to petition
Roman numeral one
es is French for 'are' in tu es

explanation.surface: The French arrive late behind a request to welcome a single constellation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting behind' places the French word after the rest of the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: The Pleiades is the star cluster in Taurus also called the Seven Sisters.

clue.text: No great lecturer getting request to repeat something

blocks.note: par is the normal level, nothing special
a don is a university teacher

explanation.surface: A mediocre academic is asked by students to say something again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pardon?' is the polite word for asking someone to say it again.
explanation.definitionFit: Said as a question, the word asks a speaker to repeat what was not heard.

clue.text: Sailor turning up in parsonage unexpectedly someone you want to see

indicators.note: in a down clue turning up reads the word from bottom to top
in places the first piece inside the second
an unexpected outcome breaks the normal pattern, so these letters come out in a fresh order

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged
a tar is a sailor

explanation.surface: A seaman arriving at the vicarage out of the blue turns out to be a welcome visitor.
explanation.definitionFit: Persona grata is Latin for an acceptable or welcome person, the opposite of persona non grata.

clue.text: Place for whoopee cushion, perhaps, after replacing a glee cushion

indicators.note: replacing moves things into new positions, so these letters are put in a different order

blocks.note: the twelve letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A prankster swaps a jolly cushion for a whoopee cushion and needs somewhere to hide it.
explanation.walkthrough: A whoopee cushion is a joke rubber bladder that makes a rude noise when sat on, so any seat is its place.
explanation.definitionFit: A chaise longue is a long upholstered couch, a seat where such a prank cushion might be left.

clue.text: One-time rat transformed into model character?

indicators.note: something transformed changes its form, so the letters take a new shape

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A former rodent changed into a figure, like a fairytale transformation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One-time rat' suggests a turncoat or Pinocchio-style story, apt since a puppet becomes a real boy there.
explanation.definitionFit: A marionette is a string puppet, a jointed figure modelled on a person or animal.

clue.text: Disorderly, on the loose, climbing into barrow

indicators.note: climbing in a down clue means going upward, so the letters read bottom to top
going into something places it inside

blocks.note: a prisoner on the loose is out
a barrow is an ancient burial mound

explanation.surface: An unruly escapee scrambles up into a wheelbarrow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'barrow' looks like a wheelbarrow but is the archaeological mound, Latin tumulus.
explanation.definitionFit: Tumultuous means noisy, confused and unruly, just like something disorderly.

clue.text: President implicating his country in exploitation?

indicators.note: to implicate is to involve or wrap up, so one piece is drawn inside the other

blocks.note: Abe is Abraham Lincoln
a president's country, the United States

explanation.surface: A head of state dragging his own nation into a scandal of misuse.
explanation.definitionFit: Abuse and exploitation both mean taking unfair advantage of someone or something.

clue.text: Accommodating description of race-track at times

blocks.note: first meaning: relaxed and tolerant
second meaning: horse-racing reports the state of the turf as the going, which can be easy

explanation.surface: A tolerant temperament compared with the state of a horse-racing course.
explanation.walkthrough: In horse racing the going is the ground condition, graded from firm to soft; 'easy' going is a natural phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: An easygoing person is relaxed and willing to fit in with others, which is what accommodating describes.

clue.text: Various hearings end in trouble for one served legal notice

indicators.note: various suggests a mixed assortment, so these letters are muddled
an end is the final letter, so only the last letter of the word is kept

blocks.note: the main letters to be rearranged
the final letter of trouble

explanation.surface: A string of court hearings ends badly for someone handed a summons.
explanation.definitionFit: A garnishee is a person or bank told by a court to hold a debtor's money for a creditor.

clue.text: I backed limits on name for tavern — something anti-inflammatory?

indicators.note: limits are the boundaries, so only the outside letters of the word are kept
going backwards means everything after the first word is written from end to start

blocks.note: taken as written
the first and last letters of name
taken as written
a pub is a tavern

explanation.surface: Someone supported limits on what a pub may be called, then wondered about a painkiller.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I backed' looks like a phrase on its own, but I stands first and 'backed' reverses all that follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Ibuprofen is a common non-steroidal drug taken to reduce swelling, pain and fever.

clue.text: Be powered by what overlong speakers do?

blocks.note: first meaning: use as fuel, as a car does petrol
second meaning: keep talking past the proper end

explanation.surface: A wry question about what drives people who talk too long.
explanation.definitionFit: A machine runs on a fuel, while a long-winded speaker continues beyond the time allowed.

clue.text: Source of power wasted in loading train

indicators.note: something wasted is ruined or wrecked, so these letters lose their order

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Electricity is squandered while freight is put onto a railway train.
explanation.walkthrough: The National Grid is Britain's high-voltage electricity transmission network.
explanation.definitionFit: Homes and businesses draw electricity from the national transmission network, so it is the supply they rely on.

clue.text: Patent finished before end of night

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter, which is all that is used

blocks.note: over means finished
the final letter of night

explanation.surface: A patent application completed just before midnight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Patent' looks like the noun for an invention licence, but it is the adjective meaning obvious.
explanation.definitionFit: Patent as an adjective means plain to see, and overt likewise means open and unconcealed.

clue.text: Unspecified number evicted from stadium neighbourhood

indicators.note: someone evicted is thrown out, so that letter is removed

blocks.note: n stands for an unspecified number in maths
an arena is a stadium

explanation.surface: An unknown number of residents thrown out of the sports ground's local district.
explanation.definitionFit: An area is a district or locality, which is what a neighbourhood is.

clue.text: Put down cards

blocks.note: first meaning: knock someone to the floor
second meaning: a pack of playing cards

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as an instruction to lay down your cards in a game, but splits into a verb and a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: To deck someone is to punch them to the ground, and a deck is a full pack of playing cards.

clue.text: Dry, requiring feed of river? Digger produced

indicators.note: a feed goes into something, so one letter is put inside the other word

blocks.note: to towel is to dry
R is the map abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: Drying a river bank needed a mechanical excavator.
explanation.definitionFit: A trowel is a small hand tool for digging in the garden, so a digger in the crossword sense.

clue.text: Veteran less good without a right hand

indicators.note: 'without' in its old sense of outside means one word goes round the others

blocks.note: worse means less good
taken as written
R is the abbreviation for right
H is the abbreviation for hand

explanation.surface: An old soldier is weaker now that he has lost a right hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking', but it means outside here.
explanation.definitionFit: A warhorse is an old campaigner, someone experienced and long in service.

clue.text: Time after time bringing in second variable substitute

indicators.note: to bring something in is to take it inside, so one letter sits within the word

blocks.note: an era is a period of time
S is the abbreviation for second
T is the abbreviation for time
algebra uses x, y and z for unknowns

explanation.surface: Time after time a second unpredictable stand-in is called on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Time after time' looks like the idiom for repeatedly; it is two separate time words placed in order.
explanation.definitionFit: Ersatz means used as an inferior replacement for the genuine article, so a substitute.

clue.text: Sound of animal having returned without a saddle

indicators.note: a sound is heard rather than read, so the word is taken by how it is said

blocks.note: a bear is an animal, and its name is said like the word for naked
to be back is to have returned

explanation.surface: The noise of a creature that has come home and has no saddle on.
explanation.definitionFit: Riding bareback means riding a horse with nothing on its back, no saddle at all.
